description: Write file storage code once. Run it against local files, S3, SFTP, or Azure. Python library with a unified Store API, swappable backends, and capability-gated methods.
rules: Use Store.read(path) for streaming reads, Store.write(path, content) for streaming writes (returns WriteResult), and Store.list_files(path) for directory listings.
Backends declare capabilities (LAZY_READ, ATOMIC_WRITE, ATOMIC_MOVE, METADATA, GLOB, ...). Query with store.supports(Capability.X); see FEATURES.md for the full matrix.
Install optional backends via pip extras: remote-store[s3], [s3-pyarrow], [sftp], [azure], [sql], [sql-query], [arrow], [dagster].
For async workloads, import AsyncStore from remote_store.aio. Wrap any sync backend with SyncBackendAdapter to expose it through the async interface.
Built-in backends: LocalBackend, MemoryBackend, ReadOnlyHttpBackend, S3Backend, S3PyArrowBackend, SFTPBackend, AzureBackend, SQLBlobBackend, SQLQueryBackend.
Streaming reads: with store.read(path) as f: data = f.read(). Atomic writes: with store.open_atomic(path) as f: f.write(...). The destination appears only after the block exits cleanly.
Errors are typed in remote_store.errors (NotFound, AlreadyExists, BackendUnavailable, CapabilityNotSupported, etc.); backends never leak SDK-native exceptions.
Configuration loads from TOML, YAML, dict, or Pydantic models via Registry; ${ENV_VAR} placeholders are resolved and credentials are wrapped in Secret automatically.

Extensions live under remote_store.ext: PyArrow filesystem adapter, Parquet datasets, batch ops, transfer ops, retry/backoff, OpenTelemetry, caching, glob fallback, integrity helpers, Dagster IO manager.
